chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The inhabitants of Mecca, when they visit the House and enter their houses, complete (the prayer), and when they do not enter their houses, shorten (the prayer).
ai.seo_question: Do residents of Mecca shorten their prayers during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a resident (*muqim*) and a traveler (*musafir*) specifically within the context of Mina, establishing that the intent to reside in one's dwelling determines the prayer length. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the physical act of entering and settling in a home transforms the status of the Meccan resident, thereby exempting them from the shortening (*qasr*) rule that applies to those camping in temporary structures. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating the varying conditions of pilgrims during the Hajj season.
